title: ENGINE OIL - SERVICING
question: During the initial 25 hours of engine operation, what type of oil should be added if necessary?
answer:
CAUTION: Incorrect use of solvent cleaners during panel replacement may lead to scratching on the wing root. Only use protective materials and ensure that ambient temperature is met before proceeding.

NOTE:  An inspection of the filter can aid in the detection of premature engine wear. Refer to Lycoming Service Bulletin 480D or latest revision.Oil Change Intervals. (1)  Airplanes are delivered from the factory with aviation grade mineral oil conforming to SAE J1966. During the first 25 hours of engine operation, it may be necessary to add oil. Use an aviation grade mineral oil of the recommended viscosity conforming to SAE J1966. After the first 25 hours, drain the engine oil and change the filter. Fill the oil sump with aviation grade mineral oil of the recommended viscosity, conforming to SAE J1966. Use it until a total of 50 hours of engine operation has occurred or oil consumption has stabilized. Then the sump must be drained and ashless dispersant oil conforming to SAE J1899, must be added to the engine. NOTE:  The turbocharged engines use only ashless dispersant oil conforming to SAE J1899, even during the engine break-in period. (2)  For other engine change intervals, refer to Chapter 5, Inspection Time Limits.

title: ENGINE OIL - SERVICING
question: What is the proper procedure for verifying the engine oil level and ensuring the correct oil type during routine maintenance after the engine has been shut down?
answer:
WARNING: Inadequate panel replacement of the engine nacelle may compromise aircraft integrity. Always wear insulated gloves, follow approved methods, and check for discoloration before returning to service.

Engine Oil Checking Procedures. Refer to Chapter 71, Engine - Description And Operation, Figure 1. (1)  Five to ten minutes after the engine has been stopped, exam the engine oil with the dipstick . The airplane must be in a level position as much as possible for the best indication. (2)  Open the engine oil door on the upper cowling. (3)  Remove the dipstick from the engine and wipe down with a clean cloth. (4)  Insert the dip stick fully and remove. (5)  Exam the oil level on the dipstick. (6)  If the oil is low, add the correct quantity and viscosity of aviation grade engine oil. NOTE:  The airplane may be operating with SAE J1966  during the initial break-in period or after an overhaul. After the break-in period, use a ashless dispersant oil conforming to SAE J1899. Make sure the proper oil type is used when servicing the engine. (7)  Insert the dipstick in the filler tube and do a check for correct seating. (8)  Close the engine oil door.

Use an aviation grade mineral oil of the recommended viscosity conforming to SAE J1966. After the first 25 hours, drain the engine oil and change the filter. Fill the oil sump with aviation grade mineral oil of the recommended viscosity, conforming to SAE J1966. Use it until a total of 50 hours of engine operation has occurred or oil consumption has stabilized. Then the sump must be drained and ashless dispersant oil conforming to SAE J1899, must be added to the engine. NOTE:  The turbocharged engines use only ashless dispersant oil conforming to SAE J1899, even during the engine break-in period. (2)  For other engine change intervals, refer to Chapter 5, Inspection Time Limits.

title: ENGINE OIL - SERVICING
question: What is the recommended procedure for verifying the engine oil level and ensuring the correct oil type during an aircraft engine inspection after shutdown?
answer:
WARNING: Inadequate panel replacement of the engine nacelle may compromise aircraft integrity. Always wear insulated gloves, follow approved methods, and check for discoloration before returning to service.

Engine Oil Checking Procedures. Refer to Chapter 71, Engine - Description And Operation, Figure 1. (1)  Five to ten minutes after the engine has been stopped, exam the engine oil with the dipstick . The airplane must be in a level position as much as possible for the best indication. (2)  Open the engine oil door on the upper cowling. (3)  Remove the dipstick from the engine and wipe down with a clean cloth. (4)  Insert the dip stick fully and remove. (5)  Exam the oil level on the dipstick. (6)  If the oil is low, add the correct quantity and viscosity of aviation grade engine oil. NOTE:  The airplane may be operating with SAE J1966  during the initial break-in period or after an overhaul. After the break-in period, use a ashless dispersant oil conforming to SAE J1899. Make sure the proper oil type is used when servicing the engine. (7)  Insert the dipstick in the filler tube and do a check for correct seating. (8)  Close the engine oil door.
